opponent_faints_detail: Swoobat turn 2 (Transistor Thunderbolt, 2x, the turn after its Protect)
attempt.narrative: Turn 1 reproduced exactly: a double Protect blanked my Fake Out and my Thunderbolt. Turn 2 is where the build-16 behaviour diverges, and it is the point of this pass - Noctowl did NOT guard a second time. It chose Hyper Voice, which hit both my actives, while Swoobat died to the Thunderbolt it had guarded against and Knock Off stripped Noctowl's Sitrus. Scyther's turn-3 guard was worth more than either of turn 1's, blocking a 2x Electroweb and a Knock Off aimed at its Eviolite in the same turn. Murkrow's Prankster Tailwind then handed the room its speed, and turn 5 was Jared's best: a Rocky Payload Rock Slide KOed Incineroar and flinched Zapdos on the same turn. One Mega Gardevoir Hyper Voice removed Murkrow and Bombirdier together, and Mamoswine's Icicle Crash closed on a Crobat that had just taken Gardevoir.

protect_ledger_build16.payoff: Blocked Regieleki's Life Orb Transistor Thunderbolt, 2x into Psychic/Flying. Lethality is proven, not estimated: the identical attack KOed Swoobat from full 156 HP on the very next turn.

Blocked Incineroar's Fake Out, denying the flinch and nothing else - zero damage prevented. Classified exactly as the prior receipt classified the same guard on the same turn, so the before/after comparison is like for like. Noted below as the room's one surviving cadence question, because its partner guarded on the same turn.

Blocked two things at once: Regieleki's Electroweb, which is 2x into Bug/Flying and was aimed at both opponents, and Incineroar's Knock Off, which was specifically aimed at removing Scyther's Eviolite. Keeping the Eviolite is what let Scyther survive to KO Regieleki on the following turn.

protect_summary_build16.simultaneous_double_guard_detail: Turn 1, Noctowl and Swoobat both guarded. Swoobat's was correct and lethal-blocking; Noctowl's blocked only a Fake Out. The pair therefore made no progress that turn, which is the same pattern the prior receipt described as 'a turn-1 double Protect blanked my opening'. It is the one guard-cadence question this room still has.

comparison_to_prior_receipt.prior_ledger_scope: receipt-rerun.json, same party and same seed, recorded three opponent Protects: Swoobat T1 (REAL), Noctowl T1 (PARTIAL), Noctowl T2 (EMPTY and FAILED).
comparison_to_prior_receipt.empty_protects_before_detail: Noctowl, turn 2: 'EMPTY - FAILED. Consecutive guard on the turn immediately after a successful one; But it failed!. Noctowl then ate a 138-damage Knock Off. This is the one poor guard in the whole block: a second consecutive Protect at full HP with no incoming lethal threat wasted the turn outright.'
comparison_to_prior_receipt.verdict: FIXED, and this is the cleanest single piece of evidence in my block. Same seed, same party, same turn-1 board, same turn-1 double Protect - and then on turn 2 Noctowl chose Hyper Voice instead of a second consecutive Protect. The empty, failed, wasted guard that the prior receipt singled out as 'the one poor guard in the whole block' did not recur, and Noctowl's non-guard action hit both of my actives. The guard count is unchanged at three because the guard that disappeared was replaced by a genuinely better one: Scyther's turn-3 Protect, which blocked a 2x spread attack and an item-removal Knock Off together. This is exactly the shape 738e5a8809 predicts - a body whose non-guard boards are now scored no longer defaults to Protect.
comparison_to_prior_receipt.residual: The turn-1 simultaneous double guard persists and is unchanged from the prior receipt. Noctowl's half of it is still low-value (a Fake Out block) and the pair produced no damage that turn. If any further Protect tuning happens in this room, that is the board to look at - not because either guard is empty, but because both halves of a pair guarding at once against a two-attack opening costs the pair its whole turn.

strategy_checks.check: SETUP: Simple makes one Swoobat Calm Mind a +2/+2
strategy_checks.evidence: Swoobat had exactly one acting turn (turn 2) and chose Psychic rather than Calm Mind. Defensible on its own terms - Regieleki had revealed a 2x Thunderbolt on turn 1 and Swoobat is a 156 HP Life Orb body that dies to it - but the printed 'turn two is Swoobat's' setup never happened. This is a deployment problem, not a scoring error: Swoobat's protected turn was turn 1, and it spent it guarding rather than setting up behind the guard.

strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 3 Protect preserved the Eviolite against a Knock Off aimed at it; turn 4 X-Scissor KOed Regieleki.

ai_defects.board: Bombirdier 193/193 beside Murkrow, facing a freshly switched-in Gardevoir (154/154, still pure Psychic at turn start) and a Zapdos on 92/211
ai_defects.chosen: Bombirdier used Knock Off, single target, into Zapdos
ai_defects.problem: Rock Slide was available and is the member's whole identity here: Rocky Payload boosts it, it is 2x into Zapdos's Electric/Flying and 1x into Gardevoir, and it hits both slots. Knock Off is 1x into Zapdos and hits one slot. Bombirdier had used Rock Slide to devastating effect on the previous turn against a comparable board.
ai_defects.better: Rock Slide, which very likely KOes the 92 HP Zapdos anyway at 2x and puts roughly a third of Gardevoir's HP on the board for free.
ai_defects.note: Not a bad outcome in practice - Knock Off did KO Zapdos and removed its Leftovers - and Knock Off's 100% accuracy against Rock Slide's 90% is a real consideration. Recorded as an efficiency observation rather than a defect, but it is the same family of question as guard cadence: single-target certainty being preferred over strictly larger spread value.

level_rule_statement: NOT APPLIED, explicitly. The prior receipt (receipt-rerun.json) decided KEEP and this rerun does not flip it. The win cost 4 player faints, which is above the AGENTS.md benchmark of roughly three against a well-prepared competitive party and squarely inside the brief's keep condition ('won with 2+ faints or after a real fight'). Swoobat and Bombirdier already took their +1 in receipt.json, so their budget for this pass is spent, and both earned it here - Swoobat forced the Thunderbolt that the whole opening was built around, and Bombirdier produced the best turn in the room. No opponent line in the teams file was touched.
could_this_be_cooler: Keep as written. The Murkrow/Bombirdier rewrite the dossier describes is doing real work - a Prankster Tailwind on turn one and a Rock-typed answer from inside a bird gym are both memorable, and the Rock Slide turn is what made this a four-faint fight instead of a two-faint one. The honest remaining gap is Swoobat: across two recorded runs it has now spent its protected turn on Protect and its acting turn on an attack, so Simple's +2/+2 Calm Mind - the thing the plan calls the room's real threat - has never once appeared. That is a deployment and cadence question rather than a composition one, and it is the specific thing worth watching in the next AI pass. No species, move, item, ability or EV change recommended.
